# SPEC: Mark expired pantry items

## Problem

`bun pantry.ts` prints each item as `<name>: <n> days`. For an item whose date
has passed, `n` is negative (e.g. `yogurt: -2 days`). People misread this and
throw out good food by mistake. Users also have no quick way to see only what
has expired.

## Definitions

- **Today**: the local date when the command runs.
- **Expired**: an item whose `expires` date is strictly before today
  (`daysLeft(...) < 0`). An item that expires today is **not** expired; it still
  shows `0 days`.

## Acceptance criteria

### AC-1: Expired items show the word EXPIRED

- **WHEN** the user runs `bun pantry.ts` and an item's `expires` date is before
  today (e.g. `yogurt` expiring `2026-11-12`, run on `2026-11-14`)
- **THEN** that item's line reads `yogurt: EXPIRED`, with no negative day count
  anywhere on the line.

### AC-2: Items not yet expired are unchanged

- **WHEN** the user runs `bun pantry.ts` and an item's `expires` date is today or
  later (e.g. `milk` expiring `2026-11-20`, or any item expiring `2026-11-14`,
  run on `2026-11-14`)
- **THEN** that item's line keeps the current format, `<name>: <n> days`
  (`milk: 6 days`, and `0 days` for an item expiring today), and does not
  contain the word `EXPIRED`.

### AC-3: `--expired` lists only expired items

- **WHEN** the user runs `bun pantry.ts --expired`
- **THEN** the output contains one `<name>: EXPIRED` line for each expired item,
  in the same order as `items.json`, and no lines for items that are not
  expired. If no item is expired, the command prints nothing and exits with
  status 0.

## Out of scope

- Deleting, archiving, or editing items.
- Colour or other styling of the output.
- Changing how `daysLeft` rounds partial days.

## Assumptions and open questions

1. **"Date has passed" means before today, not "today or before".** An item
   expiring today is still treated as usable. Please confirm.
2. **Exact wording is `<name>: EXPIRED`**, replacing the day count. The ticket
   says "show the word EXPIRED" but does not say whether the number should stay
   (e.g. `yogurt: EXPIRED (2 days ago)`).
3. **Empty `--expired` output:** printing nothing with exit 0 is assumed. A
   message such as `No expired items` is an alternative.
4. **Data mismatch:** the ticket says "3 of the 8 items in my list are already
   expired", but `items.json` in this repo has 3 items, and 1 of them
   (`yogurt`) is expired. The reporter's real list is probably different. The
   criteria above do not depend on the count.

content.text:
I found one Important problem. P-2 and P-3 meet every acceptance criterion when the clock is in UTC, but outside UTC an item can be called expired a day early or a day late. All 4 tests pass, and I didn't change any project file; I only wrote a throwaway probe script in the scratchpad. | # | Severity | Finding | Where | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | **Important** | **The expired check uses the UTC date, not the local date.** SPEC.md defines "Today" as the *local* date, but `daysLeft` compares the expiry date, read as midnight UTC, with the current moment including time of day. I ran `listItems` at two fixed moments:
• **UTC−8, 20:00 on 2026-11-14:** an item expiring today prints `today: EXPIRED`. That breaks AC-2, which says an item expiring today shows `0 days`.
• **UTC+10, 08:00 on 2026-11-14:** an item that expired yesterday prints `yest: 0 days`, and one expiring today prints `1 days`. That breaks AC-1.
This also affects `--expired`, so the wrong items can be listed or left out. The spec puts "how `daysLeft` rounds partial days" out of scope, but this is a mix-up between UTC and local dates, not rounding. It is exactly the misreading the ticket wants to stop. | `pantry.ts:8`, used by `pantry.ts:13` and `pantry.ts:22` | | 2 | Nit | **The tests can't catch finding 1.** The unit tests fix today at `2026-11-14T00:00:00Z`, which is UTC midnight, and the `--expired` test only uses dates in 2000 and 2999. So the spec's main edge case, an item expiring today, is never tested at any other time of day or in any other timezone. | `pantry.test.ts:7`, `pantry.test.ts:40-45` | | 3 | Nit | **The expired rule is written twice.** `daysLeft(...) < 0` appears in both `listItems` and the `--expired` filter. A single `isExpired(item, today)` helper would stop the two from drifting apart. | `pantry.ts:13`, `pantry.ts:22` | Everything else meets the spec: - **AC-1:** expired items print `: EXPIRED` with no number. - **AC-2:** an item expiring today prints `0 days`, not `-0`, and later items keep the ` days` format. - **AC-3:** the filter keeps the `items.json` order, prints nothing when no item is expired, and exits with status 0.
